name: PAD Open Lower Extremity Revascularization with SSI
remarks: Models the full clinical pathway for peripheral arterial disease (PAD) from initial
diagnosis through treatment strategy selection, and — for patients who receive open
lower extremity revascularization — through the 90-day surgical site infection (SSI)
outcome window.
Clinical workflow:
1a. PAD onset delay: Uniform(0, 20) years after age 60 (onset age 60-80)
1b. PAD diagnosis (ConditionOnset) — capped at age 90
2. Outpatient PAD diagnosis encounter
3. Document presenting symptom (asymptomatic, claudication, rest pain, wound/tissue loss)
4. Document comorbidities (smoking, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, CHF, functional
impairment) and anthropometrics (BMI, height, weight)
5. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement
6. End outpatient encounter
7. Treatment strategy decision:
- Medical management (40%) → Terminal
- Endovascular revascularization (30%) → Terminal
- Open surgical revascularization (30%) → SSI pathway
8. Pre-surgical workup delay (1-6 months)
9. Historical prior revascularization (25%)
10. Pre-index non-prophylaxis antibiotic (30%)
11. Urgency flag (25% urgent/emergent)
12. Inpatient surgical admission → perioperative cefazolin → open revascularization
13. Post-operative inpatient stay (3-7 days) → discharge
14. SSI risk check (comorbidity-adjusted) → SSI pathway or Terminal
Cohort definitions:
Target  : inpatient surgery for open lower extremity revascularization
Outcome : SSI diagnosis within 90 days of index surgery
SSI incidence and type assumptions:
Fixed SSI incidence after open surgery: 20%
SSI type distribution (of all SSI cases):
Superficial incisional (SNOMED 609339001) : 30% — antibiotics only, outpatient resolution
Deep incisional        (SNOMED 609340004) : 30% — readmission + operative debridement
Organ-space            (SNOMED 609341000) : 40% — readmission + operative debridement
Comorbidity prevalence assumptions in this surgical PAD population:
Current smoker                       : 35%
Type 2 diabetes mellitus             : 30%
Obesity (BMI >= 30)                  : 40%
Hypertension                         : 60%
COPD                                 : 20%
CHF                                  : 15%
Functional status (Barthel survey):
Independent transfers and ambulation : 75%
Ambulation with 1-person help        : 15%
Wheelchair bound                     : 10%
Presenting symptom distribution (Rutherford-aligned):
Asymptomatic (Rutherford 0)          : 10%
Claudication (Rutherford 1-3)        : 50%
Rest pain (Rutherford 4)             : 25%
Wound / tissue loss (Rutherford 5-6) : 15%
Treatment strategy distribution:
Medical management only              : 40%
Endovascular revascularization       : 30%
Open surgical revascularization      : 30%
Primary concept codes (OMOP-mappable):
PAD condition          : SNOMED-CT 399957001
Femoro-popliteal bypass    : SNOMED-CT 112828007
Femoral endarterectomy     : SNOMED-CT 16589005
Aortobifemoral bypass      : SNOMED-CT 405482000
Femoro-tibial bypass       : SNOMED-CT 47575002
Extra-anatomic bypass      : SNOMED-CT 73985009
SSI condition          : SNOMED-CT 433202001
Debridement (re-op)    : SNOMED-CT 225148005
Ankle-brachial index   : LOINC     77194-9
Wound culture (aerobe) : LOINC     632-0
Tobacco smoking status : LOINC     72166-2
BMI                    : LOINC     39156-5
Transferring (Barthel) : LOINC     83185-9
Ambulation (Barthel)   : LOINC     83186-7
Cefazolin (ppx)        : RxNorm    20496
Cephalexin (SSI tx)    : RxNorm    2673
Timing:
Pre-surgical workup delay : 1-6 months after PAD diagnosis
Inpatient stay            : 3-7 days post-surgery
SSI onset window          : 5-83 days post-discharge (8-90 days post-surgery)
Superficial antibiotic course  : 7-14 days (outpatient, then resolve)
Deep/organ-space antibiotic    : initiated outpatient, continued through admission
Outpatient-to-readmission gap  : 1-3 days (deep and organ-space only)
Rehospitalization stay         : 7-21 days inside inpatient encounter (deep and organ-space only)
Usage:
Copy to <synthea_home>/src/main/resources/modules/ and run Synthea normally.
To load into the omop_synth database, run this project's Step 5 CSV-to-OMOP ETL workflow against
the generated CSV output.
Does NOT model: mortality, limb loss, graft failure, or recurrent PAD.
PAD onset delay: Uniform(0, 20) years after age 60 (onset age 60-80).
Reduced from 0-50 to 0-20 years to concentrate PAD onset earlier in
post-60 life, increasing the proportion of patients whose surgery falls
within the study simulation window. Age_90_Check ensures no procedure
occurs on patients over age 90.
Cap the PAD pathway at age 90. Patients older than 90 after the
onset delay are routed to Terminal so procedure ages stay realistic.
Initial outpatient PAD evaluation encounter.
Presenting symptom, comorbidities, and ABI are all documented during this visit.
Documents presenting symptom / Rutherford class at first evaluation.
Rutherford 0: asymptomatic (10%)
Rutherford 1-3: claudication (50%)
Rutherford 4: rest pain (25%)
Rutherford 5-6: wound / tissue loss (15%)
Rutherford category 0 — no symptoms.
Rutherford categories 1-3 — claudication.
SNOMED-CT 63491006 = Intermittent claudication (OMOP concept 442774, standard).
Previous code 266261006 was incorrect: in OMOP vocabulary v5.0 (2024-10-01)
that code maps to Raynaud's phenomenon (concept 4143972), not claudication.
The correct standard SNOMED code for Intermittent claudication is 63491006.

codes.display: Peripheral vascular disease with rest pain

remarks: Rutherford category 4 — ischemic rest pain.
SNOMED-CT 428171009 = Peripheral vascular disease with rest pain
(OMOP concept 4325344, standard_concept = S).
Previous code 60389000 was incorrect: in the current OMOP vocabulary
that code maps to Paraplegia (concept 192606), not rest pain.
Concept 4325344 is also the ancestor used in the Table 1 indication
query, so this code maps directly to the query target.
Rutherford categories 5-6 — tissue loss or non-healing wound.
SNOMED-CT 238794007 = Ischemic foot ulcer
(OMOP concept 4033352, standard_concept = S).
Previous code 400012003 was incorrect: in the current OMOP vocabulary
that code maps to Abrasion and/or friction burn of skin (concept 4266654).
Concept 4033352 is a direct descendant of Ischemic ulcer (concept 4029926),
which is the ancestor used in the Table 1 tissue loss indication query.
Note: the indication query ancestor was also corrected from 319835
(Congestive heart failure — wrong) to 4029926 (Ischemic ulcer — correct).

Type 2 diabetes prevalence in PAD patients is modeled at 30%.

codes.display: Fluoroscopy guided percutaneous transluminal angioplasty of peripheral artery with contrast

remarks: Endovascular revascularization (balloon angioplasty or stenting).
Not an open surgery — does not enter the SSI outcome pathway.
Urgency is determined immediately after the treatment strategy decision.
25% of open surgical procedures are flagged urgent or emergent.
Urgent branch records an emergency-operation procedure before surgical admission.
Using type Procedure (not Observation) routes the record to synthea.procedures,
which the ETL maps into OMOP procedure_occurrence via SNOMED-CT 73994005 →
standard concept 4158569 (Emergency procedure, Procedure domain).  An Observation
type would route to synthea.observations, where the ETL only maps LOINC codes,
causing the record to be silently dropped.
Time from PAD evaluation to open revascularization surgery.
Includes pre-operative imaging, cardiac risk stratification, and scheduling.
Range: 1-6 months.
20% of admitted patients start a non-prophylactic cephalexin course at the time of
admission (e.g. pre-operative treatment of a concurrent skin/soft-tissue infection).
The course runs 3-7 days and precedes the perioperative cefazolin prophylaxis.
The remaining 80% proceed directly to the pre-operative delay and then cefazolin.
Treatment-length antibiotic course started at admission: 3-7 days.
Duration > 2 days satisfies the pipeline prolonged-antibiotic criterion.
Pre-operative optimisation window between admission and surgery: 0-7 days.
All admission paths (with or without cephalexin) merge here before the
perioperative prophylactic antibiotic and revascularisation procedure.
Single-dose perioperative cefazolin per SCIP/ACS NSQIP guidelines.
Ended immediately after the procedure.
Open lower extremity revascularization procedure selection.
Five representative procedure types with equal probability (20% each):
1. Femoro-popliteal bypass      — SNOMED 112828007
2. Femoral endarterectomy        — SNOMED 16589005
3. Aortobifemoral bypass         — SNOMED 405482000
4. Femoro-tibial bypass          — SNOMED 47575002
5. Extra-anatomic arterial bypass — SNOMED 73985009
(covers axillofemoral, axillobifemoral, and femorofemoral crossover)

remarks: Extra-anatomic arterial bypass — routes the conduit outside the normal
anatomic plane. Covers axillofemoral, axillobifemoral, and femorofemoral

SNOMED-CT 73985009 = Extra-anatomic bypass of artery
(OMOP concept_id 4307475, domain: Procedure, standard_concept = S).
Splits patients into the inpatient-SSI path vs. the standard post-op path.
Marginal SSI rate is preserved at 20%, with 30% of SSIs diagnosed during the
index inpatient stay (6% of all patients) and 70% diagnosed after discharge
(14% of all patients).
6%  -> Inpatient_SSI_Pre_Onset_Delay      (inpatient SSI subgraph)
94%  -> Post_Op_Inpatient_Delay            (post-op stay)
-> Index_Discharge_Disposition_Branch joins the post-discharge
SSI risk and the discharge-disposition decision into a single
4-way fork (rehab/home x will-SSI/no-SSI).
Time from index procedure to inpatient SSI diagnosis: post-op day 3-6.
Onset is placed before the planned discharge so the SSI condition_start_date
falls inside the surgical admission window.  The post-SSI extended LOS
(see Inpatient_SSI_Extended_LOS_*) keeps the discharge after the SSI date.
Distributes inpatient SSI cases across the three CDC/NHSN SSI classifications,
matching the 30/30/40 split used by the post-discharge SSI flow.
Standard inpatient stay after open lower extremity bypass: 3-7 days.
Reached by the 94% of patients who do NOT develop an inpatient SSI
(both the post-discharge-SSI and no-SSI paths).
Joint decision over (1) whether the patient will develop a post-discharge
SSI and (2) the discharge disposition for the index surgical admission.
Reached only by the 94% of patients who did NOT develop an inpatient SSI
(the inpatient-SSI 6% path is handled separately by
Inpatient_SSI_Discharge_Disposition).
Disposition rates (per user spec):
- rehab discharge:  30% if no SSI ever, 50% if eventual SSI
- home  discharge:  70% if no SSI ever, 50% if eventual SSI
Conditional probability of post-discharge SSI within this 94% group =
0.14 / 0.94 = 0.148936; combined with the 50/50 disposition split for
the will-SSI cases and 30/70 for the no-SSI cases gives the four joint
weights below (summing to 1.0).
Marginal SSI rate is preserved at 20% (6% inpatient + 14% post-discharge).
The legacy SSI_Fixed_Risk + Post_Discharge_Delay + Past_10_Years_Check
states are no longer reached and have been removed from this module.
Discharge to inpatient rehabilitation facility for a patient who will
go on to develop a post-discharge SSI.  NUBC code 62 maps to OMOP
UB04 Pt dis status concept 32228 (and is typically rolled up to CMS
Place of Service concept 8920 'Comprehensive Inpatient Rehabilitation
Facility' by the synthea-to-OMOP ETL standard mapping).
